summary: SCOBY-D0 exposes a clear multi-track structure. The active lead application is a low-cost retrievable bacterial-cellulose sorbent for oil-on-water cleanup. Two processing finalists have been preregistered for M1A: D3 freeze-dried BC with minimal environmentally compatible hydrophobic surface engineering as the performance lead, and D1 low-compaction air-dried BC as the cost-down challenger. Neither is an empirical winner yet. Targeted external outreach has been sent to CEDRE, Bo Yang, Qihe Chen and Hyeongmin Seo; external interest or replies do not promote evidence status.

marine_oil_sorbent.next_gate: Finish matched Stage-0 feedstock/process screen; fabricate 100x100 mm finalists; run M1A fresh-water vs artificial-seawater static test with D2 and commercial controls.

biopapyrus_and_material_process.claim_boundary: Modern BC sheet research and Egyptian lexical/process parallels do not demonstrate ancient SCOBY papyrus.

marine_promotion_gates: M1_G1 oil uptake in artificial seawater
M1_G4 >=99 percent material retrieval with no hazardous fragmentation
M1_G5 single contained press recovery if claimed
